newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian defence minister says no peace for now.
newsitem.headline: Colombian defence minister says no peace for now.

text.p: Colombia's long-running guerrilla war could claim another 50,000 lives before President Ernesto Samper leaves office in August next year, according to Defence Minister Gilberto Echeverri.

"If we don't start advancing now on the road to peace, we're going to have another 40,000 or 50,000 dead in the 16 months that remain to this government," Echeverri said during a congressional debate late on Wednesday on peace talks with the country's increasingly powerful leftist guerrillas.

Echeverri did not explain what his grim casualty estimate was based on, but National Police statistics show that 26,642 Colombians were killed last year alone -- many of them victims of their country's endemic political bloodshed.

Colombia's two leading guerrilla groups, the Marxist-led Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) and the National Liberation Army, have been fighting against the state since the mid-1960s in Latin America's longest insurgency.
The government recently called for peace talks with the two armed movements. But Echeverri said direct negotiations would not take place under the current government.
"Conversations will take place when there is a new president," he said, tacitly acknowledging that Samper was in no position to bring the rebels to the bargaining table.
The FARC and ELN have both dismissed Samper's government as "illegitimate" because of charges that he used millions of dollars in drug money to finance his 1994 election campaign.

Echeverri insisted, however, that it was time to lay the groundwork for talks and said the government would soon propose legislation creating a National Council on Peace to map strategies for reconciliation and pacification.
